wa_three_o_clock_rock.blurb: A big, clean granite slab tucked into a narrow valley outside Darrington, reached by a bumpy forest road and then a steep hike. Most of what is here is trad, on slabby, knobby faces that run from a single pitch to several, with a smaller group of bolted lines. Grades cluster in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, with a good number of low and mid 5.10s and only a few harder or easier outliers, so it suits a confident leader more than a first-timer. Part of the way in lies inside the Boulder River Wilderness, where power tools are not allowed. The road in is rough and stays open only through ongoing advocacy, so check conditions before driving up.

wa_lower_castle.blurb: The bottom half of Castle Rock, a granite face above the Wenatchee River in Tumwater Canyon, a few miles west of Leavenworth along Highway 2. Nearly all of the climbing is trad, mostly two-pitch lines that top out on Logger's Ledge, with a couple of sport and aid routes mixed in. Grades run from easy 5.6 to the 5.12 range, though most sit between 5.8 and 5.10. The rock is steep and grippy, but heavily used lines are polished. Road, river and wind noise make talking hard, so agree on rope signals. A 50 or 60 meter rope works well, and the face takes plenty of afternoon sun.
wa_lower_castle.parking_note: Use the large dirt pullout on the north side of Highway 2 in Tumwater Canyon, roughly two to two and a half miles west of the edge of Leavenworth.
wa_lower_castle.approach: From the lower, eastern end of the pullout, drop downhill about 50 yards to the climbers' trail, then follow it steeply up to the base of the wall. The lower routes start close to the car.

wa_ryan_s_wall.blurb: A gneiss sport crag in the Upper Skagit Valley, just off Highway 20 at Newhalem inside North Cascades National Park. It sits in a steep wooded valley and looks west and south. All of the routes are bolted, and the grades run hard: a few 5.10s and a thin handful of 5.9 and low 5.11s, but the bulk are 5.12 or tougher, so it is a place for strong sport climbers. The wall closes completely from March 1 to about mid July each year while peregrine falcons nest, and may reopen earlier. Sport climbing is only allowed in the park's designated climbing areas, and climbing elsewhere is prohibited.
